title: Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance - International Logistics
subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: In international logistics, what is the primary purpose of INCOTERMS (International Commercial Terms)?
options: To define the engineering standards for manufacturing products.
To establish the precise rules regarding currency exchange rates.
To define the responsibilities of buyers and sellers for the delivery of goods, including transfer of risk and allocation of transport costs.
To list the customs tariffs for every country.
questions.explain: Incoterms (e.g., EXW, FOB, DDP) are standard trade definitions used in international contracts to allocate the risks, costs, and responsibilities of transporting and clearing goods between the buyer and seller.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Under the Incoterm 'DDP' (Delivered Duty Paid), who is responsible for paying the import customs and tariffs when goods enter the buyer's country?
questions.explain: DDP (Delivered Duty Paid) places the maximum obligation on the seller. The seller is responsible for all costs and risks involved in delivering the goods to the destination, including paying any import duties and clearing customs.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Under the Incoterm 'EXW' (Ex Works), at what point does the buyer assume all risk and transportation costs?
options: Once the goods are loaded onto a ship at the seller's port.
Once the goods cross the border into the buyer's country.
Immediately when the seller makes the goods available at their own premises (factory or warehouse).
Upon final delivery to the buyer's municipal warehouse.
questions.explain: EXW (Ex Works) places the minimum responsibility on the seller. The buyer assumes all risk and costs for loading, transporting, and clearing the goods the moment they are made available at the seller's facility.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A public agency in the US buys specialized transit vehicles from Europe. The contract is priced in Euros. If the value of the US Dollar drops significantly against the Euro before the payment is due, who assumes the currency exchange risk?
questions.explain: If a contract requires a US agency to pay in a foreign currency (Euros), the buyer assumes the currency fluctuation risk. It will cost the buyer more US dollars to purchase the necessary Euros if the dollar weakens.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: To classify traded products and correctly determine the applicable customs tariffs and duties worldwide, customs authorities rely on an internationally standardized system of names and numbers. This is called:
options: The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS)
questions.explain: The Harmonized Commodity Description and Coding System (HS) is an internationally standardized system of names and numbers to classify traded products, determining the duties and taxes assessed by customs.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: An agency is purchasing complex scientific equipment from Japan. To mitigate the risk of the seller taking payment and not shipping the goods, the agency utilizes a document issued by a bank guaranteeing that the buyer's payment to the seller will be received on time and for the correct amount, provided specific shipping documents are presented. This instrument is called a:
questions.explain: A Letter of Credit (LC) is a bank-issued guarantee utilized heavily in international trade. It ensures the seller receives payment as long as they provide the bank with compliant documentation proving the goods were shipped.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A government buyer discovers that the imported electronics they intend to purchase will be subject to a 10% 'tariff'. What does this mean?
options: It is a discount applied for international diplomacy.
It is a tax imposed by the importing government on goods brought into the country, increasing the final landed cost.
It is a fee charged by the ocean freight carrier for late pickup.
It is an insurance premium mandated by maritime law.
questions.explain: A tariff is a tax or duty assessed by a government on imported goods. Tariffs increase the total cost of acquisition (the 'landed cost') and must be factored into evaluations of foreign goods.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: Which organization primarily publishes and updates the INCOTERMS used in international procurement logistics?
questions.explain: Incoterms (International Commercial Terms) are developed, published, and regularly updated by the International Chamber of Commerce (ICC).
questions.subject: CPPB Domain I: Regulatory & Compliance

questions.q: A 'Customs Broker' in an international procurement transaction acts as:
options: The primary manufacturer of the goods.
The entity that physically transports the goods across the ocean.
An agent who assists the buyer or seller in clearing goods through customs by preparing and submitting documentation and paying duties.
The bank guaranteeing the Letter of Credit.
questions.explain: A customs broker is a licensed individual or firm that assists importers and exporters in meeting federal requirements governing imports and exports, specifically managing the complex documentation, duties, and taxes required at customs.
